The **National Space Activities Commission** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales_, **CONAE**) is the civilian agency of the [government of Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Argentina "Government of Argentina") in charge of the national [space programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_program "Space program").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Sociedad Argentina Interplanetaria

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Sociedad Argentina Interplanetaria")]

During the 1940s, [Teófilo Tabanera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te%C3%B3filo_Tabanera "Teófilo Tabanera") organized a group of foreign and Argentine specialists as the Sociedad Argentina Interplanetaria, SAI (Argentine Interplanetary Society). Tabanera's efforts ensured that Argentina was the first Latin American nation to create a spaceflight organisation and in 1952 was one of the founding members of the International Astronautical Federation. Argentine Aldo Cocca was a pioneer in [space law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_law "Space law") and helped originate the idea of space being the common heritage of humankind, later enshrined in United Nations treaties of the 1960s.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-3)

### Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales")]

[![Image 8: Logo de la Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Logo_de_la_CNIE.png/120px-Logo_de_la_CNIE.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Logo_de_la_CNIE.png)

Logo Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales _[CNIE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNIE "CNIE")_

In 1960, Tabanera was named head of the newly created _Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales_ "CNIE" (National Commission for Space Research), a forerunner agency founded in 1960.

CNIE worked with the Argentine Air Force's _Instituto de Investigaciones Aeronáuticas y Espaciales_ (IIAE) to develop a number of indigenous multistage high-altitude sounding rockets and missiles ([Alfa Centauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centauro_(sounding_rocket)#Alfa_Centauro "Centauro (sounding rocket)") and [Beta Centauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centauro_(sounding_rocket)#Beta_Centauro "Centauro (sounding rocket)") in 1961, [Gamma Centauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centauro_(sounding_rocket)#Gamma_Centauro "Centauro (sounding rocket)") in 1962, [Proson-M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proson-M1 "Proson-M1") in 1963, [Orión-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ori%C3%B3n_(rocket) "Orión (rocket)") in 1965, [Orión-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ori%C3%B3n_(rocket)#Ori%C3%B3n-2 "Orión (rocket)") and [Canopus I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopus_(rocket) "Canopus (rocket)") in 1966, [Rigel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigel_(rocket) "Rigel (rocket)"), [Canopus II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopus_2 "Canopus 2") and [Castor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castor_A "Castor A") in 1969 and [Tauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tauro_(rocket) "Tauro (rocket)") in 1977).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-9) Argentina was the first country in Latin America to send an object into space using an indigenously developed rocket.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In October 1968, a committee of French studies (from the [CNES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNES "CNES")) visited the airport to conduct a survey and trace maps and planes, planning to carrying out a bi-national project called EOLO that involved launching from three bases in Argentina ([Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendoza,_Argentina "Mendoza, Argentina"), [Neuquén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuqu%C3%A9n_Province "Neuquén Province"), and [Tierra del Fuego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tierra_del_Fuego_Province,_Argentina "Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina")), small super pressure balloons which would be interrogated by a satellite during its flight. Once checked the appropriate soil conditions, in April of the following year, the Command-in-Chief of the [Argentine Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Air_Force "Argentine Air Force") formally requested to the Mendoza provincial State a grant the loan of a portion of land located in the north side of the airport, to establish the station. As requested, the province gave the land required as free loan extended for five years. After that time, the remaining facilities would be taken by the local government. The program, from the CNIE's side, was initially managed from the Argentine Air Force Condor Headquarters in Buenos Aires by EE Ingeniero Enrique Setaro. Upon the starting of the operational phase of the program the CNIE replaced him with an Air Force officer.

During the 1970s, Argentina regularly launched the American two-stage solid-propellant [Castor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castor_(rocket_stage) "Castor (rocket stage)") rocket up to 500 kilometers altitude. This rocket carried international experiments for several countries.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-10)

In the 1970s the CNIE signed an agreement with the French _Centre National d'Études Spatiales_ ([CNES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNES "CNES")) (English: National Centre for Space Studies) to create and implement the EOLO Program. It would involve the launch of 500 stratospheric air balloons into the Earth's [stratosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratosphere "Stratosphere") to study the dynamics of air displacement. The stratosphere is the second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, just above the [troposphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troposphere "Troposphere"), and below the [mesosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesosphere "Mesosphere"). The stratosphere is stratified (layered) in temperature, with warmer layers higher and cooler layers closer to the Earth; this increase of temperature with altitude is a result of the absorption of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation (shortened UV) by the [ozone layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozone_layer "Ozone layer").

### Condor Program

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Condor Program")]

In the 1980s, Argentina took part in a multinational effort to develop the [Condor missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condor_(Argentine_missile) "Condor (Argentine missile)"). Under United States pressure, the Condor program was cancelled in 1991. The associated development and production facilities at [Falda del Carmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falda_del_Carmen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Falda del Carmen (page does not exist)") were closed down, the [Fabrica Militar de Aviones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A1brica_Argentina_de_Aviones "Fábrica Argentina de Aviones"), which concentrated on development of surveillance satellites for [Earth resource](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_resource "Natural resource") and [environmental monitoring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_monitoring "Environmental monitoring").[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_][_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales")]

The present commission (CONAE) was created on 28 May 1991, during the government of [Carlos Menem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Menem "Carlos Menem"), after the cancellation of the military Condor missile program in an attempt to move all the commission efforts to civilian purposes. It received the Air Force aerospace facilities in [Córdoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina "Córdoba, Argentina") and [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires") of the former CNIE, as well as some of the civil personnel involved in the cancelled project.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since the 1990s the new commission signed agreements with [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") and European agencies and has developed a number of [Earth Observation satellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_observation_satellite "Earth observation satellite"), including SAC-A, the failed mission SAC-B, and the SAC-C launched in 2000 and still operating.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The administration of [Cristina Fernández de Kirchner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristina_Fern%C3%A1ndez_de_Kirchner "Cristina Fernández de Kirchner") renationalizes Fabrica Militar de Aviones in 2009 and the Falda del Carmen facility has been reactivated to support the development of the new [Tronador II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tronador_II "Tronador II") rocket. Defense missile and rocket development has been restarted under the umbrella of [CITEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CITEDEF "CITEDEF").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Teófilo Tabanera Space Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Teófilo Tabanera Space Center")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/74/Teofilo_Tabanera_2.JPG/250px-Teofilo_Tabanera_2.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Teofilo_Tabanera_2.JPG)

Teófilo Tabanera Space Center (CETT)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/CONAE_ANTENAS.JPG/250px-CONAE_ANTENAS.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:CONAE_ANTENAS.JPG)

Córdoba Ground Station (ETC) antennas tracking a satellite

The **Teófilo Tabanera Space Center**, or CETT (_Centro Espacial Teófilo Tabanera_), is located 30 km southwest from [Córdoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina "Córdoba, Argentina"), in a region called Falda del Carmen and houses the following installations:

### Cordoba Ground Station

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Cordoba Ground Station")]

Responsible for the tracking, command and control (TT&C) of the Argentine satellites, and for the ingestion, cataloging and archiving of satellite data products. CONAE's Córdoba Ground Station (ETC) has been in operation since 1997. It has capacity for data reception and TT&C. Currently, it receives data from 12 international satellites, besides the data from Argentine missions. The National Space Program foresees the setting up of a second ground station in [Ushuaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushuaia "Ushuaia"), Tierra del Fuego Province, at the southern tip of Argentina, to enable the collection of data on the [Antarctic continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctica "Antarctica").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-11)

### Mission Operation Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Mission Operation Center")]

Responsible for planning, commands elaboration and monitoring the Argentine satellites. Today the SAC-C Mission Operation Center is fully operative and [SAC-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-D "SAC-D") mission operation centre is being implemented in order to control the SAC-D/Aquarius satellites launched on 10 June 2011.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Testing and Integration Facilities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Testing and Integration Facilities")]

Testing and Integration Facilities are specialized spaces where different components of space missions, such as [satellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite "Satellite"), [spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft "Spacecraft"), and instruments, are tested, assembled, and integrated. These facilities play an important role in ensuring that the equipment and technology intended for [space missions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_missions "Space missions") function properly and reliably.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-12)

### Institute for Advance Space Studies "Mario Gulich"

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Institute for Advance Space Studies \"Mario Gulich\"")]

For the promotion of advanced knowledge and innovative use of space information, it also aims at developing highly skilled human resources. It has been named in honor of former CONAE physicist Mario Gulich, who conceived the first Argentine satellite for scientific applications: the SAC-B. Mr. Gulich died in 1994.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## Satellite systems

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Satellite systems")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Aquarius_SAC-D_satellite.png/250px-Aquarius_SAC-D_satellite.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Aquarius_SAC-D_satellite.png)

SAC-D

The national space program provides for two satellite series and both are devoted to [Earth observation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_observation "Earth observation"): one with main Argentine instruments in the optical range (SAC) and the other one in the [microwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microwave "Microwave") range ([SAOCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAOCOM "SAOCOM")).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-25)

### SAC series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: SAC series")]

The SAC series has been developed by the CONAE together with the Argentine company [INVAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INVAP "INVAP") and a number of local universities, in close cooperation with the NASA. It has also included the participation of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Space_Agency "Brazilian Space Agency"), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Space_Agency "Italian Space Agency") and [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Aerospace_Center "German Aerospace Center").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2019, five Argentine satellites have been launched: SAC-A, a technological demonstration satellite, SAC-B, which was devoted to scientific research, SAC-C, the first Earth Observation Satellite of Argentina, SAC-D and SAOCOM 1A.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-26)

In this context, CONAE has joined efforts with NASA in the creation of the First International Earth Observation Constellation, with Argentine SAC-C and the U.S. [Landsat 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landsat_7 "Landsat 7"), [EO-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_Observing-1 "Earth Observing-1") and [Terra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_(satellite) "Terra (satellite)") missions.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-27)

The satellite launched by CONAE was SAC-D/Aquarius, which was launched on 10 June 10, 2011.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-MSDB-28) It will carry the NASA-provided Aquarius mission for taking measurements of sea salinity which will contribute to the better understanding of the environment, together with CONAE-provided sensors which will contribute to monitoring possible fire focuses.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-29)

#### Past missions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Past missions")]

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/SAC-A.jpg/250px-SAC-A.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SAC-A.jpg)

SAC-A view from the Space Shuttle

*   [SAC-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-A?action=edit&redlink=1 "SAC-A (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-A "es:SAC-A")]: 3 December 1998 ([Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle")). Conceived to test systems and as a technological model. The satellite burned up upon entering the atmosphere on October 25, 1999.
*   [SAC-B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-B?action=edit&redlink=1 "SAC-B (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-B "es:SAC-B")]: 4 November 1996 ([Pegasus rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegasus_rocket "Pegasus rocket")). The first Argentine scientific satellite, whose main goal was the study of [solar physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_physics "Solar physics") and [astrophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrophysics "Astrophysics"). Launching problems prevented it from being deployed in orbit. As it was still attached to the rocket, it could not recharge its batteries through its solar panels and was only operated while the batteries lasted. The satellite re-entered the Earth's atmosphere on April 7, 2002.
*   [SAC-C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-C?action=edit&redlink=1 "SAC-C (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-C "es:SAC-C")]: 21 November 2000 ([Delta rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_rocket "Delta rocket")). Launched as part of the AM Constellation together with NASA's Landsat 7, TERRA and EO-1. Carried among other instruments a Multispectral Medium Resolution Scanner (MMRS), a High-Resolution Technological Camera (HRTC), a High Sensitivity Camera (HSC) and the GPS Occultation and Passive reflection Experiment (GOLPE). All instruments were provided by CONAE except GOLPE, which was provided by NASA. On 15 August 2013 communication with the satellite was suddenly lost. It had completed its primary mission and far exceeded its original five-year planned life.
*   SAC-D/Aquarius: SAC-D was launched on 19 June 2011.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-MSDB-28) Part of a cooperation program between CONAE and NASA ([Goddard Space Flight Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddard_Space_Flight_Center "Goddard Space Flight Center") and [JPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_Propulsion_Laboratory "Jet Propulsion Laboratory")). It carries seven instruments to study the environment, and a technology demonstration.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   [SAOCOM 1A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAOCOM_1A "SAOCOM 1A"): 8 October 2018 by a [Falcon 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falcon_9 "Falcon 9") of [SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX"). It is an Earth observation satellite.

## Launch vehicles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Launch vehicles")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Cohete_Tronador_II.JPG/250px-Cohete_Tronador_II.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cohete_Tronador_II.JPG)

Tronador II rocket

The [Tronador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tronador_(rocket) "Tronador (rocket)"), under development, is a multi-stage satellite launcher. It was expected to start flight tests in 2012. The T-4000 third stage test-rocket (with a diameter of 43.8 cm) is also being developed, with the current version using a liquid propellant engine of 40 kN trust.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-34) However, in the last 4 years, 1 third stage prototype and 1 first stage pre-prototype launch attempts have been unsuccessful. The last of these attempts ended with the rocket falling in the side of the launcher structure without any fire or explosion due to the rocket being loaded with only 460 kg of fuel for a short combustion in order to test the engine in flight for a few seconds, no material, human or environmental harm resulting.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-35)

## Airborne systems

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Airborne systems")]

CONAE is actually operating a self developed airborne SAR called SARAT. The radar is capable of obtaining full polarimetric [L-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L_band "L band") data with a resolution of 3 x 0.4 m. It is intended as a pre-SAOCOM test bench.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## International cooperation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: International cooperation")]

These missions will be part of the Italian-Argentine System of Satellites for Emergency Management (SIASGE), together with the Italian [COSMO-SkyMed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COSMO-SkyMed "COSMO-SkyMed") missions (see related article [Orfeo Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orfeo_Programme "Orfeo Programme")). Knowing the great advantages of combining the information provided by L and X Band radars and the convenience of a shorter revisit period, Argentina and Italy are joining efforts to develop this system, which will be fully devoted the provision of information to lessen the consequences of natural disasters.

CONAE, in July 2003, joined the [International Charter 'Space and Major Disasters'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Charter_'Space_and_Major_Disasters' "International Charter 'Space and Major Disasters'"), which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters through authorized users.

The agency secured an agreement with the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") on 24 June 2009, for the installation of a 35-m antenna and other mission support facilities at the [Pierre Auger Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Auger_Observatory "Pierre Auger Observatory"), near [Malargüe, Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malarg%C3%BCe,_Mendoza "Malargüe, Mendoza"). The facility will contribute to the ESA's [Mars Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Express "Mars Express"), [Venus Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus_Express "Venus Express"), and [Rosetta space probe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_space_probe "Rosetta space probe") projects, as well as CONAE's own, domestic research and the ESA's planned Deep Space project. One of only three such ESA installations in the world, the new antenna will create a triangulation which will allow the ESA to ensure mission coverage around the clock.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-37)

The **National Space Activities Commission** ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales_, **CONAE**) is the civilian agency of the [government of Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Argentina "Government of Argentina") in charge of the national [space programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_program "Space program").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Sociedad Argentina Interplanetaria

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Sociedad Argentina Interplanetaria")]

During the 1940s, [Teófilo Tabanera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Te%C3%B3filo_Tabanera "Teófilo Tabanera") organized a group of foreign and Argentine specialists as the Sociedad Argentina Interplanetaria, SAI (Argentine Interplanetary Society). Tabanera's efforts ensured that Argentina was the first Latin American nation to create a spaceflight organisation and in 1952 was one of the founding members of the International Astronautical Federation. Argentine Aldo Cocca was a pioneer in [space law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_law "Space law") and helped originate the idea of space being the common heritage of humankind, later enshrined in United Nations treaties of the 1960s.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-3)

### Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales")]

[![Image 8: Logo de la Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales.](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Logo_de_la_CNIE.png/120px-Logo_de_la_CNIE.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Logo_de_la_CNIE.png)

Logo Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales _[CNIE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNIE "CNIE")_

In 1960, Tabanera was named head of the newly created _Comisión Nacional de Investigaciones Espaciales_ "CNIE" (National Commission for Space Research), a forerunner agency founded in 1960.

CNIE worked with the Argentine Air Force's _Instituto de Investigaciones Aeronáuticas y Espaciales_ (IIAE) to develop a number of indigenous multistage high-altitude sounding rockets and missiles ([Alfa Centauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centauro_(sounding_rocket)#Alfa_Centauro "Centauro (sounding rocket)") and [Beta Centauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centauro_(sounding_rocket)#Beta_Centauro "Centauro (sounding rocket)") in 1961, [Gamma Centauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centauro_(sounding_rocket)#Gamma_Centauro "Centauro (sounding rocket)") in 1962, [Proson-M1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proson-M1 "Proson-M1") in 1963, [Orión-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ori%C3%B3n_(rocket) "Orión (rocket)") in 1965, [Orión-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ori%C3%B3n_(rocket)#Ori%C3%B3n-2 "Orión (rocket)") and [Canopus I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopus_(rocket) "Canopus (rocket)") in 1966, [Rigel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigel_(rocket) "Rigel (rocket)"), [Canopus II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canopus_2 "Canopus 2") and [Castor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castor_A "Castor A") in 1969 and [Tauro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tauro_(rocket) "Tauro (rocket)") in 1977).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-9) Argentina was the first country in Latin America to send an object into space using an indigenously developed rocket.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In October 1968, a committee of French studies (from the [CNES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNES "CNES")) visited the airport to conduct a survey and trace maps and planes, planning to carrying out a bi-national project called EOLO that involved launching from three bases in Argentina ([Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mendoza,_Argentina "Mendoza, Argentina"), [Neuquén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuqu%C3%A9n_Province "Neuquén Province"), and [Tierra del Fuego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tierra_del_Fuego_Province,_Argentina "Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina")), small super pressure balloons which would be interrogated by a satellite during its flight. Once checked the appropriate soil conditions, in April of the following year, the Command-in-Chief of the [Argentine Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Air_Force "Argentine Air Force") formally requested to the Mendoza provincial State a grant the loan of a portion of land located in the north side of the airport, to establish the station. As requested, the province gave the land required as free loan extended for five years. After that time, the remaining facilities would be taken by the local government. The program, from the CNIE's side, was initially managed from the Argentine Air Force Condor Headquarters in Buenos Aires by EE Ingeniero Enrique Setaro. Upon the starting of the operational phase of the program the CNIE replaced him with an Air Force officer.

During the 1970s, Argentina regularly launched the American two-stage solid-propellant [Castor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castor_(rocket_stage) "Castor (rocket stage)") rocket up to 500 kilometers altitude. This rocket carried international experiments for several countries.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-10)

In the 1970s the CNIE signed an agreement with the French _Centre National d'Études Spatiales_ ([CNES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNES "CNES")) (English: National Centre for Space Studies) to create and implement the EOLO Program. It would involve the launch of 500 stratospheric air balloons into the Earth's [stratosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratosphere "Stratosphere") to study the dynamics of air displacement. The stratosphere is the second major layer of Earth's atmosphere, just above the [troposphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troposphere "Troposphere"), and below the [mesosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesosphere "Mesosphere"). The stratosphere is stratified (layered) in temperature, with warmer layers higher and cooler layers closer to the Earth; this increase of temperature with altitude is a result of the absorption of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation (shortened UV) by the [ozone layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozone_layer "Ozone layer").

### Condor Program

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Condor Program")]

In the 1980s, Argentina took part in a multinational effort to develop the [Condor missile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condor_(Argentine_missile) "Condor (Argentine missile)"). Under United States pressure, the Condor program was cancelled in 1991. The associated development and production facilities at [Falda del Carmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falda_del_Carmen?action=edit&redlink=1 "Falda del Carmen (page does not exist)") were closed down, the [Fabrica Militar de Aviones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A1brica_Argentina_de_Aviones "Fábrica Argentina de Aviones"), which concentrated on development of surveillance satellites for [Earth resource](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_resource "Natural resource") and [environmental monitoring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_monitoring "Environmental monitoring").[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_][_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Comisión Nacional de Actividades Espaciales")]

The present commission (CONAE) was created on 28 May 1991, during the government of [Carlos Menem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Menem "Carlos Menem"), after the cancellation of the military Condor missile program in an attempt to move all the commission efforts to civilian purposes. It received the Air Force aerospace facilities in [Córdoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina "Córdoba, Argentina") and [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires") of the former CNIE, as well as some of the civil personnel involved in the cancelled project.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since the 1990s the new commission signed agreements with [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") and European agencies and has developed a number of [Earth Observation satellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_observation_satellite "Earth observation satellite"), including SAC-A, the failed mission SAC-B, and the SAC-C launched in 2000 and still operating.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The administration of [Cristina Fernández de Kirchner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristina_Fern%C3%A1ndez_de_Kirchner "Cristina Fernández de Kirchner") renationalizes Fabrica Militar de Aviones in 2009 and the Falda del Carmen facility has been reactivated to support the development of the new [Tronador II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tronador_II "Tronador II") rocket. Defense missile and rocket development has been restarted under the umbrella of [CITEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CITEDEF "CITEDEF").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Córdoba Ground Station (ETC) antennas tracking a satellite

The **Teófilo Tabanera Space Center**, or CETT (_Centro Espacial Teófilo Tabanera_), is located 30 km southwest from [Córdoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina "Córdoba, Argentina"), in a region called Falda del Carmen and houses the following installations:

### Cordoba Ground Station

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Cordoba Ground Station")]

Responsible for the tracking, command and control (TT&C) of the Argentine satellites, and for the ingestion, cataloging and archiving of satellite data products. CONAE's Córdoba Ground Station (ETC) has been in operation since 1997. It has capacity for data reception and TT&C. Currently, it receives data from 12 international satellites, besides the data from Argentine missions. The National Space Program foresees the setting up of a second ground station in [Ushuaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ushuaia "Ushuaia"), Tierra del Fuego Province, at the southern tip of Argentina, to enable the collection of data on the [Antarctic continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctica "Antarctica").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-11)

### Mission Operation Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Mission Operation Center")]

Responsible for planning, commands elaboration and monitoring the Argentine satellites. Today the SAC-C Mission Operation Center is fully operative and [SAC-D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-D "SAC-D") mission operation centre is being implemented in order to control the SAC-D/Aquarius satellites launched on 10 June 2011.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Testing and Integration Facilities are specialized spaces where different components of space missions, such as [satellites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satellite "Satellite"), [spacecraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spacecraft "Spacecraft"), and instruments, are tested, assembled, and integrated. These facilities play an important role in ensuring that the equipment and technology intended for [space missions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_missions "Space missions") function properly and reliably.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-12)

## Satellite systems

The national space program provides for two satellite series and both are devoted to [Earth observation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_observation "Earth observation"): one with main Argentine instruments in the optical range (SAC) and the other one in the [microwave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microwave "Microwave") range ([SAOCOM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAOCOM "SAOCOM")).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-25)

### SAC series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: SAC series")]

The SAC series has been developed by the CONAE together with the Argentine company [INVAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INVAP "INVAP") and a number of local universities, in close cooperation with the NASA. It has also included the participation of [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Space_Agency "Brazilian Space Agency"), [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Space_Agency "Italian Space Agency") and [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Aerospace_Center "German Aerospace Center").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2019, five Argentine satellites have been launched: SAC-A, a technological demonstration satellite, SAC-B, which was devoted to scientific research, SAC-C, the first Earth Observation Satellite of Argentina, SAC-D and SAOCOM 1A.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-26)

In this context, CONAE has joined efforts with NASA in the creation of the First International Earth Observation Constellation, with Argentine SAC-C and the U.S. [Landsat 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landsat_7 "Landsat 7"), [EO-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_Observing-1 "Earth Observing-1") and [Terra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terra_(satellite) "Terra (satellite)") missions.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-27)

The satellite launched by CONAE was SAC-D/Aquarius, which was launched on 10 June 10, 2011.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-MSDB-28) It will carry the NASA-provided Aquarius mission for taking measurements of sea salinity which will contribute to the better understanding of the environment, together with CONAE-provided sensors which will contribute to monitoring possible fire focuses.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-29)

*   [SAC-A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-A?action=edit&redlink=1 "SAC-A (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-A "es:SAC-A")]: 3 December 1998 ([Space Shuttle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle "Space Shuttle")). Conceived to test systems and as a technological model. The satellite burned up upon entering the atmosphere on October 25, 1999.
*   [SAC-B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-B?action=edit&redlink=1 "SAC-B (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-B "es:SAC-B")]: 4 November 1996 ([Pegasus rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegasus_rocket "Pegasus rocket")). The first Argentine scientific satellite, whose main goal was the study of [solar physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_physics "Solar physics") and [astrophysics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrophysics "Astrophysics"). Launching problems prevented it from being deployed in orbit. As it was still attached to the rocket, it could not recharge its batteries through its solar panels and was only operated while the batteries lasted. The satellite re-entered the Earth's atmosphere on April 7, 2002.
*   [SAC-C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-C?action=edit&redlink=1 "SAC-C (page does not exist)")[[es](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAC-C "es:SAC-C")]: 21 November 2000 ([Delta rocket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_rocket "Delta rocket")). Launched as part of the AM Constellation together with NASA's Landsat 7, TERRA and EO-1. Carried among other instruments a Multispectral Medium Resolution Scanner (MMRS), a High-Resolution Technological Camera (HRTC), a High Sensitivity Camera (HSC) and the GPS Occultation and Passive reflection Experiment (GOLPE). All instruments were provided by CONAE except GOLPE, which was provided by NASA. On 15 August 2013 communication with the satellite was suddenly lost. It had completed its primary mission and far exceeded its original five-year planned life.
*   SAC-D/Aquarius: SAC-D was launched on 19 June 2011.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-MSDB-28) Part of a cooperation program between CONAE and NASA ([Goddard Space Flight Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddard_Space_Flight_Center "Goddard Space Flight Center") and [JPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jet_Propulsion_Laboratory "Jet Propulsion Laboratory")). It carries seven instruments to study the environment, and a technology demonstration.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   [SAOCOM 1A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAOCOM_1A "SAOCOM 1A"): 8 October 2018 by a [Falcon 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falcon_9 "Falcon 9") of [SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX"). It is an Earth observation satellite.

## Launch vehicles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Launch vehicles")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6d/Cohete_Tronador_II.JPG/250px-Cohete_Tronador_II.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cohete_Tronador_II.JPG)

Tronador II rocket

The [Tronador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tronador_(rocket) "Tronador (rocket)"), under development, is a multi-stage satellite launcher. It was expected to start flight tests in 2012. The T-4000 third stage test-rocket (with a diameter of 43.8 cm) is also being developed, with the current version using a liquid propellant engine of 40 kN trust.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-34) However, in the last 4 years, 1 third stage prototype and 1 first stage pre-prototype launch attempts have been unsuccessful. The last of these attempts ended with the rocket falling in the side of the launcher structure without any fire or explosion due to the rocket being loaded with only 460 kg of fuel for a short combustion in order to test the engine in flight for a few seconds, no material, human or environmental harm resulting.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-35)

## Airborne systems

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Airborne systems")]

CONAE is actually operating a self developed airborne SAR called SARAT. The radar is capable of obtaining full polarimetric [L-band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L_band "L band") data with a resolution of 3 x 0.4 m. It is intended as a pre-SAOCOM test bench.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## International cooperation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=National_Space_Activities_Commission&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: International cooperation")]

These missions will be part of the Italian-Argentine System of Satellites for Emergency Management (SIASGE), together with the Italian [COSMO-SkyMed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COSMO-SkyMed "COSMO-SkyMed") missions (see related article [Orfeo Programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orfeo_Programme "Orfeo Programme")). Knowing the great advantages of combining the information provided by L and X Band radars and the convenience of a shorter revisit period, Argentina and Italy are joining efforts to develop this system, which will be fully devoted the provision of information to lessen the consequences of natural disasters.

CONAE, in July 2003, joined the [International Charter 'Space and Major Disasters'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Charter_'Space_and_Major_Disasters' "International Charter 'Space and Major Disasters'"), which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters through authorized users.

The agency secured an agreement with the [European Space Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Space_Agency "European Space Agency") on 24 June 2009, for the installation of a 35-m antenna and other mission support facilities at the [Pierre Auger Observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Auger_Observatory "Pierre Auger Observatory"), near [Malargüe, Mendoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malarg%C3%BCe,_Mendoza "Malargüe, Mendoza"). The facility will contribute to the ESA's [Mars Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_Express "Mars Express"), [Venus Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus_Express "Venus Express"), and [Rosetta space probe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_space_probe "Rosetta space probe") projects, as well as CONAE's own, domestic research and the ESA's planned Deep Space project. One of only three such ESA installations in the world, the new antenna will create a triangulation which will allow the ESA to ensure mission coverage around the clock.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Space_Activities_Commission#cite_note-37)
